# bollard - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bollard/0.21.0/bollard/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#bollard-an-asynchronous-rust-client-library-for-the-dockerpodman-api)Bollard: an asynchronous rust client library for the Docker/Podman API

Bollard leverages the latest [Hyper](https://github.com/hyperium/hyper) and
[Tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio) improvements for an asynchronous API containing
futures, streams and the async/await paradigm.

This library supports both [Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) and
[Podman](https://github.com/containers/podman) as first-class container runtimes, with
automatic socket discovery for rootless Podman. It features Windows support through [Named
Pipes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/ipc/named-pipes) and HTTPS support through optional
[Rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls) bindings. Serialization types for interfacing with
[Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) and [Buildkit](https://github.com/moby/buildkit) are generated through OpenAPI,
protobuf and upstream documentation.

[§](https://docs.rs#install)Install

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml` file

```
[dependencies]
bollard = "*"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#api)API

[§](https://docs.rs#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

| Use Case | Cargo.toml |
|---|---|
| Local Docker (Unix/Windows) | `bollard = "*"`(defaults work) |
| Remote Docker over HTTPS | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["ssl"] }` |
| SSH tunnel to remote Docker | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["ssh"] }` |
| BuildKit image builds | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["buildkit", "chrono"] }` |
| WebSocket container attach | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["websocket"] }` |
| Minimal binary size | `bollard = { version = "*", default-features = false, features = ["pipe"] }` |

[§](https://docs.rs#default-features)Default Features

Enabled by default:

- `http`- TCP connections to remote Docker/Podman (- `DOCKER_HOST=tcp://...`)
- `pipe`- Unix sockets and Windows named pipes

[§](https://docs.rs#transport-features)Transport Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| `http` | HTTP/TCP connector for remote Docker/Podman |
| `pipe` | Unix socket / Windows named pipe for local Docker/Podman |
| `ssh` | SSH tunnel connector |

[§](https://docs.rs#tlsssl-features)TLS/SSL Features

Choose **one** crypto provider:

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| `ssl` | [Rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls)with[ring](https://github.com/briansmith/ring)provider (recommended) |
| `aws-lc-rs` | [Rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls)with[aws-lc-rs](https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs)provider (FIPS-compliant) |
| `ssl_providerless` | [Rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls)without crypto provider (bring your own)`CryptoProvider` |
| `webpki` | Use Mozilla’s root certificates instead of OS native certs |

[§](https://docs.rs#datetime-features)DateTime Features

For timestamp support in events and logs, choose **one**:

**Note:** `chrono` and `time` are mutually exclusive.

[§](https://docs.rs#buildkit-features)BuildKit Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| `buildkit` | Full [BuildKit](https://github.com/moby/buildkit)support (includes`ssl`) |
| `buildkit_providerless` | BuildKit without bundled crypto provider |

**Note:** BuildKit requires either `chrono` or `time` feature to be enabled for timestamp handling.

[§](https://docs.rs#websocket-features)WebSocket Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| `websocket` | WebSocket support for using`attach_container_websocket`[tokio-tungstenite](https://github.com/snapview/tokio-tungstenite) |

[§](https://docs.rs#development-features)Development Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| `json_data_content` | Include raw JSON payload in deserialization errors |

[§](https://docs.rs#version)Version

The [Docker API](https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.52/) used by Bollard is using the latest
`1.52` documentation schema published by the [moby](https://github.com/moby/moby) project to
generate its serialization interface.

This library also supports [version
negotiation](https://docs.rs/bollard/latest/bollard/struct.Docker.html#method.negotiate_version),
to allow downgrading to an older API version.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#connecting-with-the-container-runtime)Connecting with the container runtime

Connect to Docker or Podman according to your architecture and security remit.

[§](https://docs.rs#local-recommended)Local (recommended)

Auto-detect the best available socket on the local machine.

```
use bollard::Docker;
Docker::connect_with_local_defaults();
```
Use the [ Docker::connect_with_local](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html#method.connect_with_local) method API to parameterise this interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#podman)Podman

Explicitly connect to Podman with automatic rootless/system socket discovery
(Unix only). Probes `$DOCKER_HOST`, then rootless Podman sockets, then the
system Podman socket, and finally falls back to the Docker socket.

```
use bollard::Docker;
Docker::connect_with_podman_defaults();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#socket)Socket

The client will connect to the standard unix socket location `/var/run/docker.sock` or Windows
named pipe location `//./pipe/docker_engine`.

```
use bollard::Docker;
#[cfg(unix)]
Docker::connect_with_socket_defaults();
```
Use the [ Docker::connect_with_socket](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html#method.connect_with_socket) method API to parameterise this interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#http)HTTP

The client will connect to the location pointed to by `DOCKER_HOST` environment variable, or
`localhost:2375` if missing.

```
use bollard::Docker;
Docker::connect_with_http_defaults();
```
Use the [ Docker::connect_with_http](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html#method.connect_with_http) method API to parameterise the interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#ssl-via-rustls)SSL via Rustls

The client will connect to the location pointed to by `DOCKER_HOST` environment variable, or
`localhost:2375` if missing.

The location pointed to by the `DOCKER_CERT_PATH` environment variable is searched for
certificates - `key.pem` for the private key, `cert.pem` for the server certificate and
`ca.pem` for the certificate authority chain.

```
use bollard::Docker;
#[cfg(feature = "ssl")]
Docker::connect_with_ssl_defaults();
```
Use the `Docker::connect_with_ssl` method API to parameterise the interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Note: all these examples need a [Tokio
Runtime](https://tokio.rs/).

[§](https://docs.rs#version-1)Version

First, check that the API is working with your server:

```
use bollard::Docker;
use futures_util::future::FutureExt;
// Use a connection function described above
// let docker = Docker::connect_...;
async move {
    let version = docker.version().await.unwrap();
    println!("{:?}", version);
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#listing-images)Listing images

To list docker images available on the Docker server:

```
use bollard::Docker;
use bollard::query_parameters::ListImagesOptionsBuilder;
use futures_util::future::FutureExt;
// Use a connection function described above
// let docker = Docker::connect_...;
async move {
    let options = ListImagesOptionsBuilder::default()
        .all(true)
        .build();
    let images = &docker.list_images(Some(options)).await.unwrap();
    for image in images {
        println!("-> {:?}", image);
    }
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#streaming-stats)Streaming Stats

To receive a stream of stats for a running container.

```
use bollard::Docker;
use bollard::query_parameters::StatsOptionsBuilder;
use futures_util::stream::TryStreamExt;
use std::default::Default;
// Use a connection function described above
// let docker = Docker::connect_...;
async move {
    let stats = &docker.stats("postgres", Some(
      StatsOptionsBuilder::default().stream(true).build()
    )).try_collect::<Vec<_>>().await.unwrap();
    for stat in stats {
        println!("{} - mem total: {:?} | mem usage: {:?}",
            stat.name.as_ref().unwrap(),
            stat.memory_stats.as_ref().unwrap().max_usage,
            stat.memory_stats.as_ref().unwrap().usage);
    }
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

Further examples are available in the [examples
folder](https://github.com/fussybeaver/bollard/tree/master/examples), or the [integration/unit
tests](https://github.com/fussybeaver/bollard/tree/master/tests).

# bollard/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/bollard.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/bollard)
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//! [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0)
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! [![circle-ci](https://circleci.com/gh/fussybeaver/bollard/tree/master.svg?style=svg)](https://circleci.com/gh/fussybeaver/bollard/tree/master)
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! [![appveyor](https://ci.appveyor.com/api/projects/status/n5khebyfae0u1sbv/branch/master?svg=true)](https://ci.appveyor.com/project/fussybeaver/boondock)
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! [![docs](https://docs.rs/bollard/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/bollard/)
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//!
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! # Bollard: an asynchronous rust client library for the Docker/Podman API
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! Bollard leverages the latest [Hyper](https://github.com/hyperium/hyper) and
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! [Tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio) improvements for an asynchronous API containing
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! futures, streams and the async/await paradigm.
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! This library supports both [Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) and
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! [Podman](https://github.com/containers/podman) as first-class container runtimes, with
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! automatic socket discovery for rootless Podman. It features Windows support through [Named
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! Pipes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/ipc/named-pipes) and HTTPS support through optional
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! [Rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls) bindings. Serialization types for interfacing with
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! [Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) and [Buildkit](https://github.com/moby/buildkit) are generated through OpenAPI,
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! protobuf and upstream documentation.
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! # Install
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! Add the following to your `Cargo.toml` file
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! ```nocompile
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! [dependencies]
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! bollard = "*"
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! ```
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! # API
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! ## Documentation
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! [API docs](https://docs.rs/bollard/).
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! ## Feature flags
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! ### Quick Start
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! | Use Case | Cargo.toml |
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! |----------|------------|
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! | Local Docker (Unix/Windows) | `bollard = "*"` _(defaults work)_ |
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! | Remote Docker over HTTPS | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["ssl"] }` |
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! | SSH tunnel to remote Docker | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["ssh"] }` |
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! | BuildKit image builds | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["buildkit", "chrono"] }` |
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! | WebSocket container attach | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["websocket"] }` |
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! | Minimal binary size | `bollard = { version = "*", default-features = false, features = ["pipe"] }` |
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! ### Default Features
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//!
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! Enabled by default:
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! - `http` - TCP connections to remote Docker/Podman (`DOCKER_HOST=tcp://...`)
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! - `pipe` - Unix sockets and Windows named pipes
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! ### Transport Features
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! | Feature | Description |
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! |---------|-------------|
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! | `http` | HTTP/TCP connector for remote Docker/Podman |
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! | `pipe` | Unix socket / Windows named pipe for local Docker/Podman |
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! | `ssh` | SSH tunnel connector |
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! ### TLS/SSL Features
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! Choose **one** crypto provider:
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! | Feature | Description |
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! |---------|-------------|
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! | `ssl` | [Rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls) with [ring](https://github.com/briansmith/ring) provider (recommended) |
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! | `aws-lc-rs` | [Rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls) with [aws-lc-rs](https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs) provider (FIPS-compliant) |
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! | `ssl_providerless` | [Rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls) without crypto provider (bring your own [`CryptoProvider`](https://docs.rs/rustls/latest/rustls/crypto/struct.CryptoProvider.html)) |
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! | `webpki` | Use Mozilla's root certificates instead of OS native certs |
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! ### DateTime Features
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! For timestamp support in events and logs, choose **one**:
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! | Feature | Description |
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! |---------|-------------|
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! | `chrono` | [Chrono](https://github.com/chronotope/chrono) date/time types |
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! | `time` | [Time 0.3](https://github.com/time-rs/time) date/time types |
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//!
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! **Note:** `chrono` and `time` are mutually exclusive.
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//!
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! ### BuildKit Features
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! | Feature | Description |
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! |---------|-------------|
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! | `buildkit` | Full [BuildKit](https://github.com/moby/buildkit) support (includes `ssl`) |
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! | `buildkit_providerless` | BuildKit without bundled crypto provider |
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//!
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! **Note:** BuildKit requires either `chrono` or `time` feature to be enabled for timestamp handling.
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! ### WebSocket Features
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//!
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//! | Feature | Description |
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! |---------|-------------|
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! | `websocket` | WebSocket support for [`attach_container_websocket`](Docker::attach_container_websocket) using [tokio-tungstenite](https://github.com/snapview/tokio-tungstenite) |
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! ### Development Features
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//!
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! | Feature | Description |
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! |---------|-------------|
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! | `json_data_content` | Include raw JSON payload in deserialization errors |
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//!
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! ## Version
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//!
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! The [Docker API](https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.52/) used by Bollard is using the latest
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! `1.52` documentation schema published by the [moby](https://github.com/moby/moby) project to
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//! generate its serialization interface.
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//!
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//! This library also supports [version
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! negotiation](https://docs.rs/bollard/latest/bollard/struct.Docker.html#method.negotiate_version),
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//! to allow downgrading to an older API version.
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//!
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! # Usage
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//!
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//! ## Connecting with the container runtime
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//!
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//! Connect to Docker or Podman according to your architecture and security remit.
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//!
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//! ### Local (recommended)
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//!
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//! Auto-detect the best available socket on the local machine.
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//!
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//! ```rust
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//! use bollard::Docker;
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//! Docker::connect_with_local_defaults();
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//! ```
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//!
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//! Use the [`Docker::connect_with_local`] method API to parameterise this interface.
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//!
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//! ### Podman
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//!
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//! Explicitly connect to Podman with automatic rootless/system socket discovery
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//! (Unix only). Probes `$DOCKER_HOST`, then rootless Podman sockets, then the
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//! system Podman socket, and finally falls back to the Docker socket.
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//!
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//! ```rust,no_run
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//! use bollard::Docker;
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//! Docker::connect_with_podman_defaults();
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//! ```
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//!
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//! ### Socket
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//!
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//! The client will connect to the standard unix socket location `/var/run/docker.sock` or Windows
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//! named pipe location `//./pipe/docker_engine`.
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//!
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//! ```rust
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//! use bollard::Docker;
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//! #[cfg(unix)]
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//! Docker::connect_with_socket_defaults();
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//! ```
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//!
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//! Use the [`Docker::connect_with_socket`] method API to parameterise this interface.
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//!
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//! ### HTTP
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//!
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//! The client will connect to the location pointed to by `DOCKER_HOST` environment variable, or
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//! `localhost:2375` if missing.
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//!
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//! ```rust
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//! use bollard::Docker;
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//! Docker::connect_with_http_defaults();
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//! ```
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//!
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//! Use the [`Docker::connect_with_http`] method API to parameterise the interface.
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//!
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//! ### SSL via Rustls
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//! The client will connect to the location pointed to by `DOCKER_HOST` environment variable, or
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//! `localhost:2375` if missing.
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//!
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//! The location pointed to by the `DOCKER_CERT_PATH` environment variable is searched for
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//! certificates - `key.pem` for the private key, `cert.pem` for the server certificate and
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//! `ca.pem` for the certificate authority chain.
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//!
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! ```rust
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//! use bollard::Docker;
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//! #[cfg(feature = "ssl")]
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//! Docker::connect_with_ssl_defaults();
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! ```
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//!
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//! Use the `Docker::connect_with_ssl` method API to parameterise the interface.
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//!
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//! ## Examples
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//!
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//! Note: all these examples need a [Tokio
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//! Runtime](https://tokio.rs/).
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//!
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//! ### Version
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//!
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//! First, check that the API is working with your server:
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//!
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//! ```rust,no_run
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//! use bollard::Docker;
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//!
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//! use futures_util::future::FutureExt;
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//!
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//! // Use a connection function described above
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//! // let docker = Docker::connect_...;
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//! # let docker = Docker::connect_with_local_defaults().unwrap();
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//!
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//! async move {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//!     let version = docker.version().await.unwrap();
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//!     println!("{:?}", version);
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//! };
[207](https://docs.rs#207)//! ```
[208](https://docs.rs#208)//!
[209](https://docs.rs#209)//! ### Listing images
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//!
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//! To list docker images available on the Docker server:
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//!
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//! ```rust,no_run
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//! use bollard::Docker;
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//! use bollard::query_parameters::ListImagesOptionsBuilder;
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//!
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//! use futures_util::future::FutureExt;
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//!
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//! // Use a connection function described above
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//! // let docker = Docker::connect_...;
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//! # let docker = Docker::connect_with_local_defaults().unwrap();
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//!
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//! async move {
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//!     let options = ListImagesOptionsBuilder::default()
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//!         .all(true)
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//!         .build();
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//!     let images = &docker.list_images(Some(options)).await.unwrap();
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//!
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//!     for image in images {
[230](https://docs.rs#230)//!         println!("-> {:?}", image);
[231](https://docs.rs#231)//!     }
[232](https://docs.rs#232)//! };
[233](https://docs.rs#233)//! ```
[234](https://docs.rs#234)//!
[235](https://docs.rs#235)//! ## Streaming Stats
[236](https://docs.rs#236)//!
[237](https://docs.rs#237)//! To receive a stream of stats for a running container.
[238](https://docs.rs#238)//!
[239](https://docs.rs#239)//! ```rust,no_run
[240](https://docs.rs#240)//! use bollard::Docker;
[241](https://docs.rs#241)//! use bollard::query_parameters::StatsOptionsBuilder;
[242](https://docs.rs#242)//!
[243](https://docs.rs#243)//! use futures_util::stream::TryStreamExt;
[244](https://docs.rs#244)//!
[245](https://docs.rs#245)//! use std::default::Default;
[246](https://docs.rs#246)//!
[247](https://docs.rs#247)//! // Use a connection function described above
[248](https://docs.rs#248)//! // let docker = Docker::connect_...;
[249](https://docs.rs#249)//! # let docker = Docker::connect_with_local_defaults().unwrap();
[250](https://docs.rs#250)//!
[251](https://docs.rs#251)//! async move {
[252](https://docs.rs#252)//!     let stats = &docker.stats("postgres", Some(
[253](https://docs.rs#253)//!       StatsOptionsBuilder::default().stream(true).build()
[254](https://docs.rs#254)//!     )).try_collect::<Vec<_>>().await.unwrap();
[255](https://docs.rs#255)//!
[256](https://docs.rs#256)//!     for stat in stats {
[257](https://docs.rs#257)//!         println!("{} - mem total: {:?} | mem usage: {:?}",
[258](https://docs.rs#258)//!             stat.name.as_ref().unwrap(),
[259](https://docs.rs#259)//!             stat.memory_stats.as_ref().unwrap().max_usage,
[260](https://docs.rs#260)//!             stat.memory_stats.as_ref().unwrap().usage);
[261](https://docs.rs#261)//!     }
[262](https://docs.rs#262)//! };
[263](https://docs.rs#263)//! ```

# Docker in bollard - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bollard/0.21.0/bollard/struct.Docker.html

`pub struct Docker { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#docker)Docker

The main interface for calling the Docker API. Construct a new Docker instance using one of the connect methods:

- `Docker::connect_with_http_defaults`- `http`feature)
- `Docker::connect_with_named_pipe_defaults`(requires- `pipe`feature, Windows only)
- `Docker::connect_with_ssl_defaults`(requires- `ssl`feature)
- `Docker::connect_with_unix_defaults`- `pipe`feature, Unix only)
- `Docker::connect_with_local_defaults`
- `Docker::connect_with_podman_defaults`
- `Docker::connect_with_ssh_defaults`(requires- `ssh`feature)

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::default::Default;
let mut filters = HashMap::new();
filters.insert("label", vec!["config-label=label-value"]);
let filters: HashMap<String, Vec<String>> = filters.into_iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), v.into_iter().map(String::from).collect())).collect();

[§](https://docs.rs#update-config)Update Config

Update an existing config.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-4)Arguments

- Config id or name as a string slice.
- [ConfigSpec](https://docs.rs/config/struct.ConfigSpec.html)struct.
- [UpdateConfigOptions](https://docs.rs/query_parameters/struct.UpdateConfigOptions.html)struct.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-4)Returns

- unit type `()`, wrapped in a Future.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use std::collections::HashMap;
use bollard::query_parameters::UpdateConfigOptionsBuilder;
let result = async move {
    let existing = docker.inspect_config("my-config").await?;
    let version = existing.version.unwrap().index.unwrap();
    let mut spec = existing.spec.unwrap().clone();
    let mut labels = HashMap::new();
    labels.insert(String::from("config-label"), String::from("label-value"));
    spec.labels = Some(labels.clone());
    let options = UpdateConfigOptionsBuilder::default()
        .version(version as i64)
        .build();
    docker.update_config("my-config", spec, options).await
};
```

[§](https://docs.rs#stream-upload-to-container)Stream Upload To Container

Stream an upload of a tar archive to be extracted to a path in the filesystem of container id.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-26)Arguments

- Optional [Upload To Container Options](https://docs.rs/query_parameters/struct.UploadToContainerOptions.html)struct.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-25)Returns

- unit type `()`, wrapped in a Future.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-26)Examples

```
use bollard::query_parameters::UploadToContainerOptionsBuilder;
use futures_util::{StreamExt, TryFutureExt};
use tokio::fs::File;
use tokio_util::io::ReaderStream;
let options = UploadToContainerOptionsBuilder::default()
    .path("/opt")
    .build();
let file = File::open("tarball.tar.gz")
    .map_ok(ReaderStream::new)
    .try_flatten_stream()
    .map(|x|x.expect("failed to stream file"));
docker
    .upload_to_container_streaming("my-container", Some(options), file)
    .await
    .expect("upload failed");
```

[§](https://docs.rs#upload-to-container)Upload To Container

Upload a tar archive to be extracted to a path in the filesystem of container id.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-27)Arguments

- Optional [Upload To Container Options](https://docs.rs/query_parameters/struct.UploadToContainerOptions.html)struct.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-26)Returns

- unit type `()`, wrapped in a Future.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-27)Examples

Uploading a tarball

```
use bollard::query_parameters::UploadToContainerOptionsBuilder;
use bollard::body_full;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Read;
let options = UploadToContainerOptionsBuilder::default()
    .path("/opt")
    .build();
let mut file = File::open("tarball.tar.gz").unwrap();
let mut contents = Vec::new();
file.read_to_end(&mut contents).unwrap();
docker
    .upload_to_container("my-container", Some(options), body_full(contents.into()))
    .await
    .expect("upload failed");
```
Uploading a stream

```
use bollard::query_parameters::UploadToContainerOptionsBuilder;
use bollard::body_try_stream;
use futures_util::{StreamExt, TryFutureExt};
use tokio::fs::File;
use tokio_util::io::ReaderStream;
let options = UploadToContainerOptionsBuilder::default()
    .path("/opt")
    .build();
let file = File::open("tarball.tar.gz")
    .map_ok(ReaderStream::new)
    .try_flatten_stream();
docker
    .upload_to_container("my-container", Some(options), body_try_stream(file))
    .await
    .expect("upload failed");
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bollard/docker.rs.html#444-447)#### pub fn [connect_with_ssl_defaults](https://docs.rs#method.connect_with_ssl_defaults)() -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Docker](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/errors/enum.Error.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bollard/docker.rs.html#444-447)

#### pub fn [connect_with_ssl_defaults](https://docs.rs#method.connect_with_ssl_defaults)() -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Docker](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/errors/enum.Error.html)>

Connect using secure HTTPS using defaults that are signalled by environment variables.

[§](https://docs.rs#defaults)Defaults

- The connection url is sourced from the `DOCKER_HOST`environment variable.
- The certificate directory is sourced from the `DOCKER_CERT_PATH`environment variable.
- Certificates are named `key.pem`,`cert.pem`and`ca.pem`to indicate the private key, the server certificate and the certificate chain respectively.
- The request timeout defaults to 2 minutes.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-32)Examples

```
use bollard::Docker;
use futures_util::future::TryFutureExt;
let connection = Docker::connect_with_ssl_defaults().unwrap();
connection.ping()
  .map_ok(|_| Ok::<_, ()>(println!("Connected!")));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

This function will panic if neither `ssl` nor `aws-lc-rs` features are activated,
or if you are using the `ssl_providerless` feature without installing the custom cryptographic
provider before with `rustls::crypto::CryptoProvider::install_default()`

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-33)Arguments

- `addr`: the connection url.
- `ssl_key`: the private key path.
- `ssl_cert`: the server certificate path.
- `ssl_ca`: the certificate chain path.
- `timeout`: the read/write timeout (seconds) to use for every hyper connection
- `client_version`: the client version to communicate with the server.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-33)Examples

```
use bollard::{API_DEFAULT_VERSION, Docker};
use std::path::Path;
use futures_util::future::TryFutureExt;
let connection = Docker::connect_with_ssl(
    "tcp://localhost:2375/",
    Path::new("/certs/key.pem"),
    Path::new("/certs/cert.pem"),
    Path::new("/certs/ca.pem"),
    120,
    API_DEFAULT_VERSION).unwrap();
connection.ping()
  .map_ok(|_| Ok::<_, ()>(println!("Connected!")));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#panics-1)Panics

This function will panic if neither `ssl` nor `aws-lc-rs` features are activated,
or if you are using the `ssl_providerless` feature without installing the custom cryptographic
provider before with `rustls::crypto::CryptoProvider::install_default()`

#### pub fn [connect_with_custom_transport](https://docs.rs#method.connect_with_custom_transport)<S: [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>>(
    transport: impl CustomTransport + 'static,
    client_addr: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<S>,
    timeout: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html),
    client_version: &[ClientVersion](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientVersion.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Docker](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/errors/enum.Error.html)>

Connect using custom transport implementation.
It has default implementation for `Fn(Request) -> Future<Output = Result<Response<hyper::body::Incoming>, Error>> + Send + Sync`

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-35)Arguments

- `transport`: transport.
- `timeout`: the read/write timeout (seconds) to use for every hyper connection
- `client_version`: the client version to communicate with the server.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use bollard::{API_DEFAULT_VERSION, Docker, BollardRequest};
use futures_util::future::TryFutureExt;
use futures_util::FutureExt;
let http_connector = hyper_util::client::legacy::connect::HttpConnector::new();
let mut client_builder = hyper_util::client::legacy::Client::builder(hyper_util::rt::TokioExecutor::new());
client_builder.pool_max_idle_per_host(0);
let client = std::sync::Arc::new(client_builder.build(http_connector));
let connection = Docker::connect_with_custom_transport(
    move |req: BollardRequest| {
        let client = std::sync::Arc::clone(&client);
        Box::pin(async move {
            let (p, b) = req.into_parts();
            // let _prev = p.headers.insert("host", host);
            // let mut uri = p.uri.into_parts();
            //uri.path_and_query = uri.path_and_query.map(|paq|
            //   uri::PathAndQuery::try_from("/docker".to_owned() + paq.as_str())
            // ).transpose().map_err(bollard::errors::Error::from)?;
            // p.uri = uri.try_into().map_err(bollard::errors::Error::from)?;
            let req = BollardRequest::from_parts(p, b);
            client.request(req).await.map_err(bollard::errors::Error::from)
        })
    },
    Some("http://my-custom-docker-server:2735"),
    4,
    bollard::API_DEFAULT_VERSION,
).unwrap();
connection.ping()
  .map_ok(|_| Ok::<_, ()>(println!("Connected!")));
```

[§](https://docs.rs#socket-discovery-order)Socket discovery order

- `$DOCKER_HOST`— if set and starts with- `unix://`, used directly.

- Rootless Podman: `/run/user/$UID/podman/podman.sock`

#### pub fn [with_request_modifier](https://docs.rs#method.with_request_modifier)<F>(self, modifier: F) -> Self

Set a request modifier callback that runs before each request.

This callback can modify the request before it is sent to the Docker Engine API.
Useful for setting `User-Agent` headers or other request modifications.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use bollard::Docker;
use http::header::{HeaderValue, USER_AGENT};
let docker = Docker::connect_with_socket_defaults()
    .unwrap()
    .with_request_modifier(|mut req| {
        req.headers_mut().insert(USER_AGENT, HeaderValue::from_static("my-app/1.0"));
        req
    });
```

[§](https://docs.rs#create-image)Create Image

Create an image by either pulling it from a registry or importing it.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-44)Arguments

- An optional [Create Image Options](https://docs.rs/query_parameters/struct.CreateImageOptions.html)struct.
- An optional request body consisting of a tar or tar.gz archive, or a stream
containing the root file system for the image. If this argument is used,
the value of the `from_src`option must be “-”.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-36)Returns

- [Create Image Info](https://docs.rs/config/struct.CreateImageInfo.html), wrapped in an asynchronous Stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-52)Examples

```
use bollard::query_parameters::CreateImageOptionsBuilder;
let options = CreateImageOptionsBuilder::default()
    .from_image("hello-world")
    .build();
docker.create_image(Some(options), None, None);
// do some other work while the image is pulled from the docker hub...
```
[§](https://docs.rs#unsupported)Unsupported

- Import from tarball

[§](https://docs.rs#build-image)Build Image

Build an image from a tar archive with a `Dockerfile` in it.

The `Dockerfile` specifies how the image is built from the tar archive. It is typically in
the archive’s root, but can be at a different path or have a different name by specifying
the `dockerfile` parameter.

By default, the call to build specifies using BuilderV1, the first generation builder in docker daemon.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-54)Arguments

- [Build Image Options](https://docs.rs/query_parameters/struct.BuildImageOptions.html)struct.
- Optional [Docker Credentials](https://docs.rs/auth/struct.DockerCredentials.html)struct.
- Tar archive compressed with one of the following algorithms: identity (no compression),
gzip, bzip2, xz. Optional [Hyper Body](https://docs.rs/http-body/1.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/http_body/trait.Body.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-46)Returns

- [Create Image Info](https://docs.rs/config/struct.CreateImageInfo.html), wrapped in an asynchronous Stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-62)Examples

Sending a tarball:

```
use bollard::query_parameters::BuildImageOptionsBuilder;
use bollard::body_full;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Read;
let options = BuildImageOptionsBuilder::default()
    .dockerfile("Dockerfile")
    .t("my-image")
    .rm(true)
    .build();
let mut file = File::open("tarball.tar.gz").unwrap();
let mut contents = Vec::new();
file.read_to_end(&mut contents).unwrap();
docker.build_image(options, None, Some(body_full(contents.into())));
```
Sending a stream:

```
use bollard::query_parameters::BuildImageOptionsBuilder;
use bollard::body_stream;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Read;
let options = BuildImageOptionsBuilder::default()
    .dockerfile("Dockerfile")
    .t("my-image")
    .rm(true)
    .build();
docker.build_image(options, None, Some(body_stream(stream)));
```

[§](https://docs.rs#export-image)Export Image

Get a tarball containing all images and metadata for a repository.

The root of the resulting tar file will contain the file “manifest.json”. If the export is
of an image repository, rather than a single image, there will also be a `repositories` file
with a JSON description of the exported image repositories.
Additionally, each layer of all exported images will have a sub directory in the archive
containing the filesystem of the layer.

See the [Docker API documentation](https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.52/#operation/ImageGet)
for more information.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-56)Arguments

- The `image_name`string referring to an individual image and tag (e.g. alpine:latest)

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-48)Returns

- An uncompressed TAR archive

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bollard/image.rs.html#888-899)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bollard/image.rs.html#888-899)

[§](https://docs.rs#export-images)Export Images

Get a tarball containing all images and metadata for several image repositories. Shared layers will be deduplicated.

See the [Docker API documentation](https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.52/#tag/Image/operation/ImageGetAll)
for more information.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-57)Arguments

- The `image_names`Vec of image names.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-49)Returns

- An uncompressed TAR archive

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bollard/image.rs.html#957-988)

[§](https://docs.rs#import-image)Import Image

Load a set of images and tags into a repository.

For details on the format, see the [export image
endpoint](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html#method.export_image).

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-58)Arguments

- [Image Import Options](https://docs.rs/query_parameters/struct.ImportImageOptions.html)struct.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-50)Returns

- [Build Info](https://docs.rs/config/struct.BuildInfo.html), wrapped in an asynchronous Stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-64)Examples

```
use bollard::query_parameters::ImportImageOptionsBuilder;
use bollard::errors::Error;
use bollard::body_full;
use futures_util::stream::{StreamExt, TryStreamExt};
use tokio::fs::File;
use tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt;
use tokio_util::codec;
let options = ImportImageOptionsBuilder::default()
    .build();
async move {
    let mut file = File::open("tarball.tar.gz").await.unwrap();
    let mut byte_stream = codec::FramedRead::new(file, codec::BytesCodec::new()).map(|r| {
        let bytes = r.unwrap().freeze();
        Ok::<_, Error>(bytes)
    });
    let bytes = byte_stream.next().await.unwrap().unwrap();
    let mut stream = docker
        .import_image(
            ImportImageOptionsBuilder::default().build(),
            body_full(bytes),
            None,
        );
    while let Some(response) = stream.next().await {
        // ...
    }
};
```

[§](https://docs.rs#install-plugin)Install Plugin

Pull and install a plugin from a registry. Returns a stream of progress info.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-77)Arguments

- [InstallPluginOptions](https://docs.rs/query_parameters/struct.InstallPluginOptions.html)struct.
- Vector of [PluginPrivilege](https://docs.rs/config/struct.PluginPrivilege.html)to grant (from[get_plugin_privileges](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html#method.get_plugin_privileges)).
- Optional [Docker Credentials](https://docs.rs/auth/struct.DockerCredentials.html)struct for registry authentication.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-69)Returns

- A Stream of [CreateImageInfo](https://docs.rs/config/struct.CreateImageInfo.html)(contains progress/status/error info).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-83)Examples

```
use bollard::query_parameters::{GetPluginPrivilegesOptionsBuilder, InstallPluginOptionsBuilder};
use futures_util::stream::TryStreamExt;
// First get the required privileges
let priv_opts = GetPluginPrivilegesOptionsBuilder::default()
    .remote("vieux/sshfs:latest")
    .build();
let privileges = docker.get_plugin_privileges(priv_opts).await?;
// Then install with those privileges
let options = InstallPluginOptionsBuilder::default()
    .remote("vieux/sshfs:latest")
    .name("my-sshfs-plugin")
    .build();
let mut stream = docker.install_plugin(options, privileges, None);
while let Some(info) = stream.try_next().await? {
    println!("{:?}", info);
}
```

Update an existing secret, fails when more than one service use that secret or trying update data.

- Secret id or name as a string slice.
- [SecretSpec](https://docs.rs/config/struct.SecretSpec.html)struct.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-78)Returns

- unit type `()`, wrapped in a Future.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-92)Examples

```
use std::collections::HashMap;
use bollard::query_parameters::UpdateSecretOptionsBuilder;
let result = async move {
    let existing = docker.inspect_secret("my-secret").await?;
    let version = existing.version.unwrap().index.unwrap();
    let mut spec = existing.spec.unwrap().clone();
    let mut labels = HashMap::new();
    labels.insert(String::from("secret-label"), String::from("label-value"));
    spec.labels = Some(labels.clone());
    let options = UpdateSecretOptionsBuilder::default()
        .version(version as i64)
        .build();
    docker.update_secret("my-secret", spec, options).await
};
```

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-89)Returns

- unit type `()`, wrapped in a Future.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-103)Examples

```
use bollard::query_parameters::UpdateSwarmOptionsBuilder;
let result = async move {
    let swarm = docker.inspect_swarm().await?;
    let version = swarm.version.unwrap().index.unwrap();
    let spec = swarm.spec.unwrap();
    let options = UpdateSwarmOptionsBuilder::default()
        .version(version as i64)
        .build();
    docker.update_swarm(spec, options).await
};
```

# bollard::config - Rust

Config API: manage and inspect docker configs within a swarm

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html)
- Address represents an IPv4 or IPv6 IP address.
- [Auth](https://docs.rs/struct.AuthConfig.html)- Config
- [Auth](https://docs.rs/struct.AuthResponse.html)- Response
- An identity token was generated successfully.
- [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html)
- Volume configuration

- BuildCache contains information about a build cache record.

- represents system data usage for build cache resources.
- [Build](https://docs.rs/struct.BuildIdentity.html)- Identity
- BuildIdentity contains build reference information if image was created via build.
- [Build](https://docs.rs/struct.BuildInfo.html)- Info
- [Build](https://docs.rs/struct.BuildPruneResponse.html)- Prune - Response
- [Cluster](https://docs.rs/struct.ClusterInfo.html)- Info
- ClusterInfo represents information about the swarm as is returned by the "/info" endpoint. Join-tokens are not included.
- [Cluster](https://docs.rs/struct.ClusterVolume.html)- Volume
- Options and information specific to, and only present on, Swarm CSI cluster volumes.
- [Cluster](https://docs.rs/struct.ClusterVolumeInfo.html)- Volume - Info

- [Cluster](https://docs.rs/struct.ClusterVolumeSpec.html)- Volume - Spec
- Cluster-specific options used to create the volume.

- [Cluster](https://docs.rs/struct.ClusterVolumeSpecAccessModeAccessibilityRequirements.html)- Volume - Spec - Access - Mode - Accessibility - Requirements
- Requirements for the accessible topology of the volume. These fields are optional. For an in-depth description of what these fields mean, see the CSI specification.
- [Cluster](https://docs.rs/struct.ClusterVolumeSpecAccessModeCapacityRange.html)- Volume - Spec - Access - Mode - Capacity - Range
- The desired capacity that the volume should be created with. If empty, the plugin will decide the capacity.
- [Cluster](https://docs.rs/struct.ClusterVolumeSpecAccessModeSecrets.html)- Volume - Spec - Access - Mode - Secrets
- One cluster volume secret entry. Defines a key-value pair that is passed to the plugin.
- [Commit](https://docs.rs/struct.Commit.html)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.Config.html)

- The config-only network source to provide the configuration for this network.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigSpec.html)- Spec
- [Container](https://docs.rs/struct.ContainerBlkioStatEntry.html)- Blkio - Stat - Entry
- Blkio stats entry. This type is Linux-specific and omitted for Windows containers.
- [Container](https://docs.rs/struct.ContainerBlkioStats.html)- Blkio - Stats
- BlkioStats stores all IO service stats for data read and write.  This type is Linux-specific and holds many fields that are specific to cgroups v1. On a cgroup v2 host, all fields other than `io_service_bytes_recursive`are omitted or`null`. This type is only populated on Linux and omitted for Windows containers.
- [Container](https://docs.rs/struct.ContainerConfig.html)- Config

- [Container](https://docs.rs/struct.ContainerInspectResponse.html)- Inspect - Response
- [Container](https://docs.rs/struct.ContainerMemoryStats.html)- Memory - Stats

- [Container](https://docs.rs/struct.ContainerPidsStats.html)- Pids - Stats

- [Object](https://docs.rs/struct.ObjectVersion.html)- Version
- The version number of the object such as node, service, etc. This is needed to avoid conflicting writes. The client must send the version number along with the modified specification when updating these objects. This approach ensures safe concurrency and determinism in that the change on the object may not be applied if the version number has changed from the last read. In other words, if two update requests specify the same base version, only one of the requests can succeed. As a result, two separate update requests that happen at the same time will not unintentionally overwrite each other.

# bollard::models - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bollard/0.21.0/bollard/models/index.html

## Expand description

Re-exported request body and response types from `bollard-stubs`.

Use these types directly from `bollard::models` instead of adding `bollard-stubs`
as a dependency. This ensures version compatibility and simplifies your dependencies.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use bollard::Docker;
use bollard::models::ContainerCreateBody;
use bollard::query_parameters::CreateContainerOptionsBuilder;
let docker = Docker::connect_with_socket_defaults()?;
let config = ContainerCreateBody {
    image: Some("alpine:latest".to_string()),
    ..Default::default()
};
let options = CreateContainerOptionsBuilder::default()
    .name("my_container")
    .build();
docker.create_container(Some(options), config).await?;
```

- [Node](https://docs.rs/struct.NodeStatus.html)- Status
- NodeStatus represents the status of a node. It provides the current status of the node, as seen by the manager.
- [NriInfo](https://docs.rs/struct.NriInfo.html)
- Information about the Node Resource Interface (NRI). This field is only present if NRI is enabled.
- [Object](https://docs.rs/struct.ObjectVersion.html)- Version
- The version number of the object such as node, service, etc. This is needed to avoid conflicting writes. The client must send the version number along with the modified specification when updating these objects. This approach ensures safe concurrency and determinism in that the change on the object may not be applied if the version number has changed from the last read. In other words, if two update requests specify the same base version, only one of the requests can succeed. As a result, two separate update requests that happen at the same time will not unintentionally overwrite each other.
- [OciDescriptor](https://docs.rs/struct.OciDescriptor.html)
- A descriptor struct containing digest, media type, and size, as defined in the [OCI Content Descriptors Specification](https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/v1.0.1/descriptor.md).
- [OciPlatform](https://docs.rs/struct.OciPlatform.html)
- Describes the platform which the image in the manifest runs on, as defined in the [OCI Image Index Specification](https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/v1.0.1/image-index.md).

- [Object](https://docs.rs/struct.ObjectVersion.html)- Version
- The version number of the object such as node, service, etc. This is needed to avoid conflicting writes. The client must send the version number along with the modified specification when updating these objects. This approach ensures safe concurrency and determinism in that the change on the object may not be applied if the version number has changed from the last read. In other words, if two update requests specify the same base version, only one of the requests can succeed. As a result, two separate update requests that happen at the same time will not unintentionally overwrite each other.

# bollard::query_parameters - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bollard/0.21.0/bollard/query_parameters/index.html

## Expand description

Re-exported query parameter types from `bollard-stubs`.

Use these types directly from `bollard::query_parameters` instead of adding
`bollard-stubs` as a dependency. Each API method has a corresponding options
builder (e.g., `CreateContainerOptionsBuilder`, `ListImagesOptionsBuilder`).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use bollard::Docker;
use bollard::query_parameters::ListContainersOptionsBuilder;
let docker = Docker::connect_with_socket_defaults()?;
let options = ListContainersOptionsBuilder::default()
    .all(true)
    .build();
let containers = docker.list_containers(Some(options)).await?;
```
Method, error and parameter types for the endpoint.

- [Object](https://docs.rs/struct.ObjectVersion.html)- Version
- The version number of the object such as node, service, etc. This is needed to avoid conflicting writes. The client must send the version number along with the modified specification when updating these objects. This approach ensures safe concurrency and determinism in that the change on the object may not be applied if the version number has changed from the last read. In other words, if two update requests specify the same base version, only one of the requests can succeed. As a result, two separate update requests that happen at the same time will not unintentionally overwrite each other.

# ClientVersion in bollard - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bollard/0.21.0/bollard/struct.ClientVersion.html

## Expand description

Advisory version stub to use for communicating with the Server. The docker server will error if a higher client version is used than is compatible with the server. Beware also, that the docker server will return stubs for a higher version than the version set when communicating.

See also [negotiate_version](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html#method.negotiate_version), and the `client_version` argument when instantiating the
[Docker](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html) client instance.

# bollard - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bollard/latest/bollard/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#bollard-an-asynchronous-rust-client-library-for-the-dockerpodman-api)Bollard: an asynchronous rust client library for the Docker/Podman API

Bollard leverages the latest [Hyper](https://github.com/hyperium/hyper) and
[Tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio) improvements for an asynchronous API containing
futures, streams and the async/await paradigm.

This library supports both [Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) and
[Podman](https://github.com/containers/podman) as first-class container runtimes, with
automatic socket discovery for rootless Podman. It features Windows support through [Named
Pipes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/ipc/named-pipes) and HTTPS support through optional
[Rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls) bindings. Serialization types for interfacing with
[Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) and [Buildkit](https://github.com/moby/buildkit) are generated through OpenAPI,
protobuf and upstream documentation.

[§](https://docs.rs#install)Install

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml` file

```
[dependencies]
bollard = "*"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#api)API

[§](https://docs.rs#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

| Use Case | Cargo.toml |
|---|---|
| Local Docker (Unix/Windows) | `bollard = "*"`(defaults work) |
| Remote Docker over HTTPS | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["ssl"] }` |
| SSH tunnel to remote Docker | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["ssh"] }` |
| BuildKit image builds | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["buildkit", "chrono"] }` |
| WebSocket container attach | `bollard = { version = "*", features = ["websocket"] }` |
| Minimal binary size | `bollard = { version = "*", default-features = false, features = ["pipe"] }` |

[§](https://docs.rs#default-features)Default Features

Enabled by default:

- `http`- TCP connections to remote Docker/Podman (- `DOCKER_HOST=tcp://...`)
- `pipe`- Unix sockets and Windows named pipes

[§](https://docs.rs#transport-features)Transport Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| `http` | HTTP/TCP connector for remote Docker/Podman |
| `pipe` | Unix socket / Windows named pipe for local Docker/Podman |

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#connecting-with-the-container-runtime)Connecting with the container runtime

Connect to Docker or Podman according to your architecture and security remit.

[§](https://docs.rs#local-recommended)Local (recommended)

Auto-detect the best available socket on the local machine.

```
use bollard::Docker;
Docker::connect_with_local_defaults();
```
Use the [ Docker::connect_with_local](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html#method.connect_with_local) method API to parameterise this interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#podman)Podman

Explicitly connect to Podman with automatic rootless/system socket discovery
(Unix only). Probes `$DOCKER_HOST`, then rootless Podman sockets, then the
system Podman socket, and finally falls back to the Docker socket.

```
use bollard::Docker;
Docker::connect_with_podman_defaults();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#socket)Socket

The client will connect to the standard unix socket location `/var/run/docker.sock` or Windows
named pipe location `//./pipe/docker_engine`.

```
use bollard::Docker;
#[cfg(unix)]
Docker::connect_with_socket_defaults();
```
Use the [ Docker::connect_with_socket](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html#method.connect_with_socket) method API to parameterise this interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#http)HTTP

The client will connect to the location pointed to by `DOCKER_HOST` environment variable, or
`localhost:2375` if missing.

```
use bollard::Docker;
Docker::connect_with_http_defaults();
```
Use the [ Docker::connect_with_http](https://docs.rs/struct.Docker.html#method.connect_with_http) method API to parameterise the interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#ssl-via-rustls)SSL via Rustls

The client will connect to the location pointed to by `DOCKER_HOST` environment variable, or
`localhost:2375` if missing.

The location pointed to by the `DOCKER_CERT_PATH` environment variable is searched for
certificates - `key.pem` for the private key, `cert.pem` for the server certificate and
`ca.pem` for the certificate authority chain.

```
use bollard::Docker;
#[cfg(feature = "ssl")]
Docker::connect_with_ssl_defaults();
```
Use the `Docker::connect_with_ssl` method API to parameterise the interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Note: all these examples need a [Tokio
Runtime](https://tokio.rs/).

[§](https://docs.rs#version-1)Version

First, check that the API is working with your server:

```
use bollard::Docker;
use futures_util::future::FutureExt;
// Use a connection function described above
// let docker = Docker::connect_...;
async move {
    let version = docker.version().await.unwrap();
    println!("{:?}", version);
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#listing-images)Listing images

To list docker images available on the Docker server:

```
use bollard::Docker;
use bollard::query_parameters::ListImagesOptionsBuilder;
use futures_util::future::FutureExt;
// Use a connection function described above
// let docker = Docker::connect_...;
async move {
    let options = ListImagesOptionsBuilder::default()
        .all(true)
        .build();
    let images = &docker.list_images(Some(options)).await.unwrap();
    for image in images {
        println!("-> {:?}", image);
    }
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#streaming-stats)Streaming Stats

To receive a stream of stats for a running container.

```
use bollard::Docker;
use bollard::query_parameters::StatsOptionsBuilder;
use futures_util::stream::TryStreamExt;
use std::default::Default;
// Use a connection function described above
// let docker = Docker::connect_...;
async move {
    let stats = &docker.stats("postgres", Some(
      StatsOptionsBuilder::default().stream(true).build()
    )).try_collect::<Vec<_>>().await.unwrap();
    for stat in stats {
        println!("{} - mem total: {:?} | mem usage: {:?}",
            stat.name.as_ref().unwrap(),
            stat.memory_stats.as_ref().unwrap().max_usage,
            stat.memory_stats.as_ref().unwrap().usage);
    }
};
```

# async-stream 0.3.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/async-stream/^0.3.5

# Asynchronous streams for Rust

Asynchronous stream of elements.

Provides two macros, `stream!` and `try_stream!`, allowing the caller to
define asynchronous streams of elements. These are implemented using `async`
& `await` notation. This crate works without unstable features.

The `stream!` macro returns an anonymous type implementing the [ Stream](https://docs.rs/futures-core/*/futures_core/stream/trait.Stream.html)
trait. The

`Item` associated type is the type of the values yielded from the
stream. The `try_stream!` also returns an anonymous type implementing the
[trait, but the](https://docs.rs/futures-core/*/futures_core/stream/trait.Stream.html)

`Stream``Item` associated type is `Result<T, Error>`. The
`try_stream!` macro supports using `?` notation as part of the
implementation.## Usage

A basic stream yielding numbers. Values are yielded using the `yield`
keyword. The stream block must return `()`.

```
use stream;
use pin_mut;
use StreamExt;
async
```
Streams may be returned by using `impl Stream<Item = T>`:

```
use stream;
use Stream;
use pin_mut;
use StreamExt;
async
```
Streams may be implemented in terms of other streams - `async-stream` provides `for await`
syntax to assist with this:

```
use stream;
use Stream;
use pin_mut;
use StreamExt;
async
```
Rust try notation (`?`) can be used with the `try_stream!` macro. The `Item`
of the returned stream is `Result` with `Ok` being the value yielded and
`Err` the error type returned by `?`.

```
use ;
use try_stream;
use Stream;
use io;
use SocketAddr;
```
## Implementation

The `stream!` and `try_stream!` macros are implemented using proc macros.
The macro searches the syntax tree for instances of `yield $expr` and
transforms them into `sender.send($expr).await`.

The stream uses a lightweight sender to send values from the stream
implementation to the caller. When entering the stream, an `Option<T>` is
stored on the stack. A pointer to the cell is stored in a thread local and
`poll` is called on the async block. When `poll` returns.
`sender.send(value)` stores the value that cell and yields back to the
caller.

## Supported Rust Versions

The current minimum supported Rust version is 1.65.

This project is licensed under the [MIT license](https://docs.rs/LICENSE).

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted
for inclusion in `async-stream` by you, shall be licensed as MIT, without any
additional terms or conditions.

# base64 0.22.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/base64/^0.22

Made with CLion. Thanks to JetBrains for supporting open source!

It's base64. What more could anyone want?

This library's goals are to be *correct* and *fast*. It's thoroughly tested and widely used. It exposes functionality at
multiple levels of abstraction so you can choose the level of convenience vs performance that you want,
e.g. `decode_engine_slice` decodes into an existing `&mut [u8]` and is pretty fast (2.6GiB/s for a 3 KiB input),
whereas `decode_engine` allocates a new `Vec<u8>` and returns it, which might be more convenient in some cases, but is
slower (although still fast enough for almost any purpose) at 2.1 GiB/s.

See the [docs](https://docs.rs/base64) for all the details.

## FAQ

### I need to decode base64 with whitespace/null bytes/other random things interspersed in it. What should I do?

Remove non-base64 characters from your input before decoding.

If you have a `Vec` of base64, [retain](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.retain) can be used to
strip out whatever you need removed.

If you have a `Read` (e.g. reading a file or network socket), there are various approaches.

- Use [iter_read](https://crates.io/crates/iter-read)together with`Read`'s`bytes()`to filter out unwanted bytes.
- Implement `Read`with a`read()`impl that delegates to your actual`Read`, and then drops any bytes you don't want.

### I need to line-wrap base64, e.g. for MIME/PEM.

[line-wrap](https://crates.io/crates/line-wrap) does just that.

### I want canonical base64 encoding/decoding.

First, don't do this. You should no more expect Base64 to be canonical than you should expect compression algorithms to
produce canonical output across all usage in the wild (hint: they don't).
However, [people are drawn to their own destruction like moths to a flame](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/361), so here we
are.

There are two opportunities for non-canonical encoding (and thus, detection of the same during decoding): the final bits
of the last encoded token in two or three token suffixes, and the `=` token used to inflate the suffix to a full four
tokens.

The trailing bits issue is unavoidable: with 6 bits available in each encoded token, 1 input byte takes 2 tokens, with the second one having some bits unused. Same for two input bytes: 16 bits, but 3 tokens have 18 bits. Unless we decide to stop shipping whole bytes around, we're stuck with those extra bits that a sneaky or buggy encoder might set to 1 instead of 0.

The `=` pad bytes, on the other hand, are entirely a self-own by the Base64 standard. They do not affect decoding other
than to provide an opportunity to say "that padding is incorrect". Exabytes of storage and transfer have no doubt been
wasted on pointless `=` bytes. Somehow we all seem to be quite comfortable with, say, hex-encoded data just stopping
when it's done rather than requiring a confirmation that the author of the encoder could count to four. Anyway, there
are two ways to make pad bytes predictable: require canonical padding to the next multiple of four bytes as per the RFC,
or, if you control all producers and consumers, save a few bytes by requiring no padding (especially applicable to the
url-safe alphabet).

All `Engine` implementations must at a minimum support treating non-canonical padding of both types as an error, and
optionally may allow other behaviors.

## Rust version compatibility

The minimum supported Rust version is 1.48.0.

All this means that it takes me a fair amount of time to review each PR, so it might take quite a while to carve out the free time to give each PR the attention it deserves. I will get to everyone eventually!

## no_std

This crate supports no_std. By default the crate targets std via the `std` feature. You can deactivate
the `default-features` to target `core` instead. In that case you lose out on all the functionality revolving
around `std::io`, `std::error::Error`, and heap allocations. There is an additional `alloc` feature that you can activate
to bring back the support for heap allocations.

# bitflags 2.13.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitflags/^2.6.0

# bitflags

`bitflags` generates flags enums with well-defined semantics and ergonomic end-user APIs.

You can use `bitflags` to:

- provide more user-friendly bindings to C APIs where flags may or may not be fully known in advance.
- generate efficient options types with string parsing and formatting support.

You can't use `bitflags` to:

-
guarantee only bits corresponding to defined flags will ever be set. `bitflags`allows access to the underlying bits type so arbitrary bits may be set.
-
define bitfields. `bitflags`only generates types where set bits denote the presence of some combination of flags.

## Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "2.13.0"
```
and this to your source code:

```
use bitflags;
```
## Example

Generate a flags structure:

```
use bitflags;
// The `bitflags!` macro generates `struct`s that manage a set of flags.
bitflags!
```
## Cargo features

The `bitflags` library defines a few Cargo features that you can opt-in to:

- `std`: Implement the- `Error`trait on error types used by- `bitflags`.
- `serde`: Support deriving- `serde`traits on generated flags types.
- `arbitrary`: Support deriving- `arbitrary`traits on generated flags types.
- `bytemuck`: Support deriving- `bytemuck`traits on generated flags types.

Also see [ bitflags_derive](https://github.com/bitflags/bitflags-derive) for other flags-aware traits.

## Rust Version Support

The minimum supported Rust version is documented in the `Cargo.toml` file.
This may be bumped in minor releases as necessary.

# Buildkit rust proto

```

```

package `protobuf-compiler` or equivalent.

# bytes 1.12.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bytes/^1

# Bytes

A utility library for working with bytes.

## Usage

To use `bytes`, first add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "1"
```
Next, add this to your crate:

```
use ;
```
## no_std support

To use `bytes` with no_std environment, disable the (enabled by default) `std` feature.

```
[]
 = {  = "1",  = false }
```
To use `bytes` with no_std environment without atomic CAS, such as thumbv6m, you also need to enable
the `extra-platforms` feature. See the [documentation for the  portable-atomic
crate](https://docs.rs/portable-atomic) for more information.

The MSRV when `extra-platforms` feature is enabled depends on the MSRV of `portable-atomic`.

## Serde support

Serde support is optional and disabled by default. To enable use the feature `serde`.

```
[]
 = {  = "1",  = ["serde"] }
```
The MSRV when `serde` feature is enabled depends on the MSRV of `serde`.

## Building documentation

When building the `bytes` documentation the `docsrs` option should be used, otherwise
feature gates will not be shown. This requires a nightly toolchain:

```
RUSTDOCFLAGS="--cfg docsrs" cargo +nightly doc
```

# chrono 0.4.45 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/chrono/^0.4

[Chrono](https://docs.rs/chrono): Timezone-aware date and time handling

Chrono aims to provide all functionality needed to do correct operations on dates and times in the
[proleptic Gregorian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proleptic_Gregorian_calendar):

- The `DateTime`
- Operations that may produce an invalid or ambiguous date and time return `Option`or`MappedLocalTime`
- Configurable parsing and formatting with an `strftime`inspired date and time formatting syntax.
- The `Local`
- Types and operations are implemented to be reasonably efficient.

Timezone data is not shipped with chrono by default to limit binary sizes. Use the companion crate
[Chrono-TZ](https://crates.io/crates/chrono-tz) or [ tzfile](https://crates.io/crates/tzfile) for
full timezone support.

## Documentation

See [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/) for the API reference.

## Limitations

- Only the proleptic Gregorian calendar (i.e. extended to support older dates) is supported.
- Date types are limited to about +/- 262,000 years from the common epoch.
- Time types are limited to nanosecond accuracy.
- Leap seconds can be represented, but Chrono does not fully support them.
See [Leap Second Handling](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/naive/struct.NaiveTime.html#leap-second-handling).

## Crate features

Default features:

- `alloc`: Enable features that depend on allocation (primarily string formatting).
- `std`: Enables functionality that depends on the standard library. This is a superset of- `alloc`and adds interoperation with standard library types and traits.
- `clock`: Enables reading the local timezone (- `Local`). This is a superset of- `now`.
- `now`: Enables reading the system time (- `now`).
- `wasmbind`: Interface with the JS Date API for the- `wasm32`target.

Optional features:

- `serde`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [serde](https://github.com/serde-rs/serde).
- `rkyv`: Deprecated, use the- `rkyv-*`features.
- `rkyv-16`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [rkyv](https://github.com/rkyv/rkyv), using 16-bit integers for integral- `*size`types.
- `rkyv-32`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [rkyv](https://github.com/rkyv/rkyv), using 32-bit integers for integral- `*size`types.
- `rkyv-64`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [rkyv](https://github.com/rkyv/rkyv), using 64-bit integers for integral- `*size`types.
- `rkyv-validation`: Enable rkyv validation support using- `bytecheck`.
- `arbitrary`: Construct arbitrary instances of a type with the Arbitrary crate.
- `unstable-locales`: Enable localization. This adds various methods with a- `_localized`suffix. The implementation and API may change or even be removed in a patch release. Feedback welcome.
- `oldtime`: This feature no longer has any effect; it used to offer compatibility with the- `time`0.1 crate.

Note: The `rkyv{,-16,-32,-64}` features are mutually exclusive.

## Rust version requirements

The Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) is currently **Rust 1.62.0**.

The MSRV is explicitly tested in CI. It may be bumped in minor releases, but this is not done lightly.

# home 0.5.12 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/home/^0.5

Canonical definitions of `home_dir`, `cargo_home`, and `rustup_home`.

This provides the definition of `home_dir` used by Cargo and rustup,
as well functions to find the correct value of `CARGO_HOME` and
`RUSTUP_HOME`.

The definition of [ home_dir](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/env/fn.home_dir.html) provided by the standard library is
incorrect because it considers the

`HOME` environment variable on
Windows. This causes surprising situations where a Rust program will
behave differently depending on whether it is run under a Unix
emulation environment like Cygwin or MinGW. Neither Cargo nor rustup
use the standard library's definition - they use the definition here.**Note:** This has been fixed in Rust 1.85 to no longer use the `HOME`
environment variable on Windows. If you are still using this crate for the
purpose of getting a home directory, you are strongly encouraged to switch to
using the standard library's [ home_dir](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/env/fn.home_dir.html) instead. It is planned to have the
deprecation notice removed in 1.87.

This crate further provides two functions, `cargo_home` and
`rustup_home`, which are the canonical way to determine the location
that Cargo and rustup store their data.

See [rust-lang/rust#43321](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/43321).

This crate is maintained by the Cargo team, primarily for use by Cargo and Rustup and not intended for external use. This crate may make major changes to its APIs or be deprecated without warning.

## License

MIT OR Apache-2.0

A protective and efficient HTTP library for all.

- HTTP/1 and HTTP/2
- Asynchronous design
- Leading in performance
- Tested and **correct**
- Extensive production use
- Client and Server APIs

**Get started** by looking over the [guides](https://hyper.rs/guides/1/).

## "Low-level"

hyper is a relatively low-level library, meant to be a building block for libraries and applications.

If you are looking for a convenient HTTP client, then you may wish to consider
[reqwest](https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest).

If you are not sure what HTTP server to choose, then you may want to consider
[axum](https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum) or
[warp](https://github.com/seanmonstar/warp), the latter taking a more functional
approach. Both are built on top of this library.

# log 0.4.33 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/log/^0.4

# log

A Rust library providing a lightweight logging *facade*.

A logging facade provides a single logging API that abstracts over the actual logging implementation. Libraries can use the logging API provided by this crate, and the consumer of those libraries can choose the logging implementation that is most suitable for its use case.

## Minimum supported `rustc`

See the `rust-version` field in `Cargo.toml` for the current minimum Rust toolchain version.

This version is explicitly tested in CI and may be bumped in any release as needed. Maintaining compatibility with older compilers is a priority though, so the bar for bumping the minimum supported version is set very high. Any changes to the supported minimum version will be called out in the release notes.

## Usage

### In libraries

Libraries should link only to the `log` crate, and use the provided macros to
log whatever information will be useful to downstream consumers:

```
[]
 = "0.4"
```
```
use ;
```
### In executables

In order to produce log output, executables have to use a logger implementation compatible with the facade. There are many available implementations to choose from, here are some options:

- Simple minimal loggers:
- Complex configurable frameworks:
- Adaptors for other facilities:
- For WebAssembly binaries:
- For dynamic libraries:
- You may need to construct [an FFI-safe wrapper over](https://github.com/rust-lang/log/issues/421)to initialize in your libraries.`log`

- You may need to construct
- Utilities:

Executables should choose a logger implementation and initialize it early in the runtime of the program. Logger implementations will typically include a function to do this. Any log messages generated before the logger is initialized will be ignored.

The executable itself may use the `log` crate to log as well.

## Structured logging

If you enable the `kv` feature, you can associate structured data with your log records:

```
use ;
```

# num 0.4.3 - Docs.rs

# num

A collection of numeric types and traits for Rust.

This includes new types for big integers, rationals (aka fractions), and complex numbers,
new traits for generic programming on numeric properties like `Integer`,
and generic range iterators.

`num` is a meta-crate, re-exporting items from these sub-crates:

| Repository | Crate | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| `num-bigint` | ||
| `num-complex` | ||
| `num-integer` | ||
| `num-iter` | ||
| `num-rational` | ||
| `num-traits` | ||
| ( )`num-derive` |

Note: `num-derive` is listed here for reference, but it's not directly included
in `num`.  This is a `proc-macro` crate for deriving some of `num`'s traits.

## Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.4"
```
## Features

This crate can be used without the standard library (`#![no_std]`) by disabling
the default `std` feature. Use this in `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.4"
 = false
```
The `num-bigint` crate requires the `std` feature, or the `alloc` feature may
be used instead with Rust 1.36 and later. Other sub-crates may also have
limited functionality when used without `std`.

The `libm` feature uses pure-Rust floating point implementations in `no_std`
builds, enabling the `Float` trait and related `Complex` methods.

The `rand` feature enables randomization traits in `num-bigint` and
`num-complex`.

The `serde` feature enables serialization for types in `num-bigint`,
`num-complex`, and `num-rational`.

The `num` meta-crate no longer supports features to toggle the inclusion of
the individual sub-crates.  If you need such control, you are recommended to
directly depend on your required crates instead.

## Releases

## Compatibility

The `num-traits`, `num-integer`, and `num-iter` crates are individually tested
for rustc 1.8 and greater, if you require such older compatibility.

# openssh 0.11.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/openssh/^0.11.5

Scriptable SSH through OpenSSH.

This crate wraps the OpenSSH remote login client (`ssh` on most machines), and provides
a convenient mechanism for running commands on remote hosts. Since all commands are executed
through the `ssh` command, all your existing configuration (e.g., in `.ssh/config`) should
continue to work as expected.

The library's API is modeled closely after that of [`std::process::Command`], since `ssh` also
attempts to make the remote process seem as much as possible like a local command.
